title: The Living God
note:
Built from the three curriculum photographs in Drive’s “01 - Curriculum Source” for Primary / Chapter 18 — the opener (p.85), the lesson (p.86) and its close with the five questions (p.87) — and the memory-verse page (p.88) in “06 - Memory Verse”.

**The three curriculum pages were not read by eye.** Each photograph is about 7 MB, past what the Drive connector can hand over to this session, so their text came from Drive’s own extraction of the images instead. It came back clean for this chapter. The memory-verse page is smaller and *was* read by eye, so the verse does not rest on extraction.

**The book names the book two ways.** The opener on p.85 says “1 Kings 18: 22-40” and the memory-verse page on p.88 says “1 King 18: 39”, without the s. Each is kept where it is printed — the chapter reference above from p.85, the verse reference from p.88 — rather than silently harmonised. Worth a teacher’s eye.

**No artwork yet.** “04 - Story Artwork” is empty, so the story is thirty-two text cards and nothing carries a picture.

The story cards render the people’s cry with commas — “The Lord, he is God!” — while the memory verse keeps the em dashes the verse page prints. The verse is the thing to hold exactly; the card is the thing to read aloud.

The chapter has two prayers. The opener on p.85 is “O God, teach us that You alone are God and You alone are to be worshipped. Make us more convinced of this truth with each lesson we learn. Amen.”; the close on p.88 is the one carried in `prayer` below.

story.text: God loved the people of Israel very much.
But they were often disobedient to Him.
They would worship Baal instead of the living God.
They began to deny the God who had been with them.
There was only one prophet of Jehovah left.
It was Elijah.
But there were four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal.
They abused and mocked Elijah all the time.
Elijah asked the people of Israel to gather at Mount Carmel.
“Get two bulls for us.”
“Let Baal’s prophets choose one and lay it on the wood.”
“But they must not set fire to it.”
“I will prepare the other bull the same way.”
“Then you call on your god, and I will call on the Lord.”
“The god who answers by fire — he is God.”
Baal’s prophets took their bull and prepared it.
They called on Baal from morning until noon.
“O Baal, answer us!”
But there was no response, and no one answered.
Then Elijah repaired the fallen altar of Jehovah.
He laid his bull on it, cut into pieces.
A moat was made around the altar.
Water was poured over the offering and the stream around it.
Elijah prayed to the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel.
“Answer me, Lord, so these people will know that you are God.”
What a miracle!
God suddenly sent a great fire.
It consumed the offering, the wood and the soil.
Even the water in the stream was drained away.
When all the people saw this, they fell down and cried out.
“The Lord, he is God! The Lord, he is God!”
If God is with us and we believe, victory will be ours.

curriculum.source: Primary Mar Thoma Vol-1, Chapter 18 “THE LIVING GOD”, p.87 — “ANSWER THE QUESTIONS”
curriculum.note:
Five questions and no “Mark it as Right or Wrong”. Every answer is from the printed lesson on pp.86–87. The page also sets “Colour the picture”, which is a pencil activity and has no game here.

**The curriculum pages were read by Drive’s own text extraction rather than by eye** — see the chapter note.

questions.question: Who was the only prophet of Jehovah who stood firm when everyone else went after Baal?
questions.objective: Know that Elijah was the only prophet of Jehovah left.
questions.answer: Elijah. “There was only one prophet of Jehovah. It was Elijah.” (p.86)

questions.question: How many prophets did Baal have?
Where did Elijah gather the people of Israel?
questions.objective: Know that Elijah gathered them at Mount Carmel.
questions.answer: Mount Carmel. “Elijah asked the people of Israel to gather at Mount Carmel.” (p.86)

questions.question: Was the prayer of Baal’s prophets answered?
questions.objective: Know that it was not: they called from morning until noon, and there was no response and no one answered.
questions.answer: No. “The prophets of Baal … called upon the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, ‘O Baal, answer us!’ But there was no response, and no one answered.” (p.86)

questions.question: How did God answer Elijah’s prayer?
questions.objective: Know that God sent a great fire that consumed the offering, the wood and the soil, and even dried the water in the stream.
questions.answer: With fire. “God suddenly sent a great fire and consumed Elijah’s burnt offering, wood, and soil. Even the water in the surrounding stream was drained away.” (pp.86–87)

games.title: One Against Many
games.objective: Know that Elijah was the only prophet of Jehovah left.

interactions.prompt: Who was the only prophet of Jehovah left?

games.note: Question 1, and the one choosing game in five. “Elisha” is the near miss worth having — one letter and one generation away — and Abraham and Isaac are in the chapter too, inside Elijah’s own prayer.

games.title: The Count and the Place
games.objective: Know that Baal had 450 prophets and that Elijah gathered Israel at Mount Carmel.

interactions.prompt: Match each one to what it was.
interactions.hint: One side was very much larger.

to.label: The god who answers by fire

games.note: Questions 2 and 3, together, because they are two halves of one picture: four hundred and fifty on one side, one man on the other, and a mountain where everybody could see. A `match` holds the odds where two separate quizzes would lose them.

games.title: Morning Until Noon
games.objective: Know that Baal's prophets called all morning and that there was no response and no one answered.

interactions.prompt: Say what you think. Then we will look.

statements.source: The prophets of Baal called on their god from morning until noon.
statements.ask: Did Baal’s prophets call from morning till noon?
statements.because: Yes. They called on the name of Baal from morning until noon.

statements.source: Baal sent fire down on the offering his prophets had made.
statements.ask: Did Baal send fire on their offering?
statements.because: No. There was no response, and no one answered.

statements.source: Elijah chose his bull first and left the other for Baal’s prophets.
statements.ask: Did Elijah choose his bull first?
statements.because: No. He let Baal’s prophets choose one for themselves.

statements.source: Water was poured over Elijah’s offering before he prayed.
statements.ask: Was water poured over Elijah’s offering?
statements.because: Yes. Water was poured over the sacrifice and the stream around it.

games.note: Question 4. The printed answer is a no, and a true-or-not is the one mechanic that can ask a no without making the child wrong for saying it. Statements 2 and 3 are written from false sentences, so each `ask` keeps that polarity and the honest answer stays “no”.

games.title: Building the Altar
games.objective: Follow what Elijah did before he prayed, so that the fire falls on a soaking altar.

interactions.hint: The water came last of all.

items.label: He laid the bull on it
A moat was made around it

games.note:
The fifth game, answering no question of its own — the Primary band wants four to five and the book’s five questions filled four.

What it carries is the thing that makes the fire mean anything: Elijah soaked the altar first. A child who has not followed that order has watched a fire light some dry wood.

games.title: The Fire Falls
games.objective: Know what God's fire consumed when it answered Elijah.

interactions.prompt: Turn over what the fire took.

items.label: Even the water in the stream

games.note: Question 5. A `reveal`, because the answer is a list of four things the fire took and the fourth — the water in the moat — is the one that settles it. Making a child pick one and calling the other three wrong would undo the point.

verse.text: When all the people saw this, they fell prostrate and cried, “The Lord—he is God! The Lord—he is God!”.

practice.hint: What they saw, what they did, and then what they said — twice.
words: When all the people saw this,
practice.note: Stage 1, phrase ordering, cut by hand around the em dashes: “Lord—he” carries no space, so a join there would not spell the verse. The build checks the pieces spell it exactly.

practice.hint: One word for how they went to the ground.
practice.note: Stage 2, the missing word with the sentence whole around it. “Down” is the near miss worth having: it is what a child would say, and it is not the word the verse uses.

practice.hint: Not Elijah — everyone who had come to watch.
practice.note: Stage 3. The whole weight of the verse is in who said it: the crowd that had gone after Baal, not the one man who had not.

practice.hint: Six pieces, and the cry comes twice.
practice.note: Stage 4, full reconstruction — six pieces where stage 1 had four.

practice.prompt: Where does our verse come from?
practice.hint: It is inside this chapter’s own Bible portion.
practice.note: Stage 5, the reference chosen against near misses. All three are inside this chapter’s own portion — 22 is where it begins and 40 is where it ends. The spelling “1 King” is the memory-verse page’s own; see the chapter note.

verse.note:
Read from p.88 through the Memory Verse agent: `--fetch --source-dir` over the memory-verse page, the supervised read, then `--from-extraction`. That page is small enough to read by eye, and was.

Five stages in the shape Primary Chapters 2 to 16 use. The agent’s own draft is a single `arrange-words` rung; the other four stages are built by hand on top of it.

The closing mark is the book’s: p.88 prints … God!”. with the full stop outside the quotation, and that is carried over unchanged.

The reference is printed “1 King 18: 39”, without the s, and is kept exactly so even though the chapter’s own opener says “1 Kings”. See the chapter note.

Translation is unresolved: p.88 does not name one.

No second opinion — the teacher’s editorial Sheet was not available for this run.

decision.statement: I will depend only on my God, no matter how many opponents come in life, I will hold fast and worship only the true God.
decision.note: The curriculum’s own My Decision from p.88, first person and unchanged — including the comma splice the book prints.

song.note: The Song on p.88, in the Latin script the book prints it in. Not translated and not completed.

prayer.text: No matter how many people come against me, no matter who tempts me to deny God, help me to depend on You alone. Amen.
prayer.note: The closing Prayer from p.88, word for word.

celebration.message: The fire fell, and all the people cried that the Lord is God.
celebration.note: The end of the lesson on pp.86–87, which is also the chapter’s memory verse.
